observations.deficiency: Procedures to ensure that sampling methods are adequate for their intended use have not been adequately established.
observations.detail: Specifically, the firm’s procedures for establishing sample sizes in validation activities lack clear guidance on when an external standard (such as an ANSI/ISO sampling requirement) can override or replace the organization’s own internal criteria. The procedures do not specify the necessary elements such as acceptance criteria, justification, rationale, approval process, methodology, or how to resolve any conflict between the two sources. Consequently, the choice of sample size in validation studies may be unsupported by statistical justification and applied inconsistently. For example: A sample size of six was initially selected in Protocol (DT_DVP0007 01) Manual Cleaning Validation Plan on the suggestion as per ANSI/AAMI ST98: 2022 [9]. ANSI/AAMI ST98: 2022. This sample size was changed to 9, a more conservative sample size, as reflected in the validation report DT_DVROOO7 03 Manual Cleaning Validation Report. Collectively, these validation reports did not adequately document the following: e the factors considered when selecting the initial six-unit size (expert judgment, industry practice, risk assessment, etc.). e the rationale or explanation why a sample size of 9 was sufficient, even if recommended by the standard that could include a clear, risk-based rationale for the sample size used, is sufficient for the specific device, process and risk level, and explain the deviation from your own internal SOP.

deterministic_detail.body: DMRC reference number DMRC-41407584 Marketing Authorisation Holder Star Pharmaceuticals Ltd Medicine Details Enalapril maleate/Hydrochlorothiazide 20 mg/12.5 mg Tablets PLPI: 20636/1651 Active ingredient: enalapril maleate / hydrochlorothiazide GTIN: 05050114165107 Affected Lot Batch Numbers Batch No. Expiry Date Pack Size First Distributed Y018198 30/06/2027 28 22/09/2026 Y019635 31/10/2027 28 05/12/2025 C125483 29/02/2028 28 05/03/2026 C135541 30/11/2028 28 08/06/2026 Background Star Pharmaceuticals Limited have informed the MHRA of a typographical error on the strength of hydrochlorothiazide printed on the front face of the carton which incorrectly states “12. mg” instead of “12.5 mg”. The strength is correctly presented on all other faces of the carton, the leaflet and the blister foil. The volume of affected stock distributed to the UK market is 1740 packs. Advice for Healthcare Professionals: Healthcare professionals are asked to note the information in this notification and should continue to dispense this product; the quality of the tablets is not impacted by this labelling defect. The risk associated with the labelling error is considered low because no corresponding strengths of the enalapril maleate / hydrochlorothiazide combination where the hydrochlorothiazide strength is expressed as 12 mg exist. Healthcare professionals are advised to reassure patients, if contacted, that the product is enalapril maleate 20 mg / hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg tablets as described in the Patient Information Leaflet. Advice for Healthcare Professionals to Provide to Patients: Patients should continue to take this medication as prescribed. This does not affect the quality of the tablets. If you are unsure or have any questions, please seek advice from your pharmacy or other healthcare professionals involved in your treatment. Patients who experience adverse reactions or have any questions about their medication should seek medical attention. Any suspected adverse reactions should also be reported via the MHRA Yellow Card scheme . Additional information: For all medical information enquiries and information on this product, please email info@drugsrus.co.uk or telephone 020 8423 2111. Recipients of this Medicines Notification should bring it to the attention of relevant contacts by copy of this notice. NHS regional teams are asked to forward this to community pharmacists and dispensing general practitioners for information.
